purpose: Structured FTC Yellowstone refund ledger distinguishing verified prior-check cashing from later payment distribution while preserving the underlying business recovery, residual loss, and exit stages as open.

events.geography: United States; small businesses harmed by Yellowstone Capital merchant cash advances
events.date_precision: Month precision; FTC refund page identifies June 2026, but no announcement day is retained; third distribution after June 2022 and August 2024 distributions
events.denominator: 3,759 small businesses receiving a third check; recipients had cashed a previous check; no business-level recovery denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from the official FTC Yellowstone Capital refund page
events.missingness: Business identifiers, individual refund amounts, underlying account correction, remaining loss, operating status, employment, customer continuity, trust, switching, and exit are not retained
events.exposure: FTC alleged Yellowstone withdrew money from business bank accounts after businesses had repaid the full amounts owed in merchant cash advance contracts
events.alternatives_before_action: Businesses could seek bank intervention, dispute withdrawals, pursue legal or complaint routes, or continue operating under the affected financing relationship; individual alternatives are not published
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: The FTC reports a third distribution totaling more than $549,000 to 3,759 businesses that had cashed a previous check; the prior cashing is an aggregate receipt signal, not a complete loss-recovery measure
events.choice_or_response: Businesses previously cashed a refund check and were eligible for an additional distribution; ongoing use, switching, or non-use of the financing relationship is not observed
events.person_or_actor_with_control: FTC and refund administrator control distribution; Yellowstone controlled the original withdrawal process; businesses control whether and how to use available financial alternatives within unknown constraints
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: FTC refund administration issued a third payment after two earlier distributions, conditioned on prior check cashing
events.remedy_receipt: FTC explicitly reports that the 3,759 recipients cashed a previous check; receipt of the third check is not yet verified in the public announcement
events.durability_followup: The FTC's 2024 annual refund report records 4,982 businesses who had cashed at least one payment, including 4,981 in the August 2024 additional distribution; the June 2026 third-check cashing rate and underlying account correction, residual loss, business survival, employment, customer continuity, and later financial security remain unknown
events.immediate_outcome: A repeat refund route reaches a previously cashing recipient group
events.protected_outcome: Some businesses received prior cash refunds and were offered additional compensation; restored liquidity or operating security is not established
events.sacrificed_outcome: Unauthorized withdrawals and any residual loss after partial refunds remain unmeasured
events.cost_risk_transfer: Repeated refund administration can return money while businesses retain uncertainty about the original financing relationship, residual loss, and future liquidity
events.later_outcome: No business-level recovery, continued financing use, switching, employment, customer service, trust, or exit endpoint is reported
events.meaning_and_attribution: No business-owner fairness, blame, institutional trust, or collective-action endpoint is observed
events.public_or_collective_response: FTC enforcement and repeat distribution are visible; business organizing or later political action is not observed
events.counterexample: Prior check cashing is stronger than a mere payment offer, but it does not establish that the third payment arrived or that the underlying financial harm was removed
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official FTC Yellowstone Capital refund announcement, rechecked 2026-09-25, and the FTC 2024 Annual Report on Refunds to Consumers, https://www.ftc.gov/system/files/ftc_gov/pdf/ftc-refunds-consumers-2024.pdf. The annual report records 4,982 businesses who had cashed at least one payment and 4,981 in the August 12, 2024 additional distribution, totaling $3,309,280 in that distribution and $6,404,871 returned in previous distributions. The current page says a June 2026 third round is being sent and instructs recipients to cash within 90 days; aggregate administration does not expose business-level third-check cashing, account correction, recovery, or later outcomes

arrows.evidence: The FTC describes the alleged withdrawals, settlement, and three refund rounds
arrows.counterexample: The public case record does not identify the original withdrawal, repayment, or settlement effect for each business

arrows.evidence: The FTC states that the 3,759 businesses receiving the third distribution had cashed a previous check; the 2024 annual refund report separately records 4,982 businesses who had cashed at least one payment and 4,981 in the August 2024 additional distribution
arrows.counterexample: Previous cashing does not verify the amount received, adequacy, or third-check receipt
arrows.remaining_gap: Recipient-level payment amounts, dates, and third-check cashing

arrows.to: restored business liquidity and operating security
arrows.evidence: The FTC reports refund amounts and prior cashing but no business operating or account outcome
arrows.counterexample: A cashed refund can coexist with residual loss, debt, closure, or continued dependence
arrows.remaining_gap: Account correction, residual loss, survival, employment, and customer continuity

arrows.to: trust, switching, continued use, or exit
arrows.evidence: The official refund page provides no later business-level behavioral or trust follow-up
arrows.counterexample: Receiving money does not reveal whether the business stayed, switched financing, or changed institutional judgment
arrows.remaining_gap: Same-business later use, switching, trust, collective action, and exit

arrows.from: third refund checks sent to previously cashing recipients
arrows.evidence: The FTC says it is sending the third checks and instructs recipients to cash them within 90 days; the public announcement does not report later cashing, while the 2024 report documents prior cashing for the earlier distribution
arrows.counterexample: Eligibility based on a prior cashed check does not establish receipt or cashing of the new check
arrows.remaining_gap: Third-check delivery, cashing, amount, timing, and any failed or returned payment

boundary: This ledger adds one official consumer-financial remedy case with an explicit prior-cashing condition. It advances recipient-side receipt evidence beyond a payment offer, but it does not establish third-payment receipt, adequate recovery, account correction, business survival, trust, switching, or exit.
storage_boundary: Only compact official page-derived fields, source URL, and uncertainty are retained; no business identifiers, administrator file, or raw payment file is downloaded.
